result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A gives a complete, consistent token set. Its prose and wide columns share one centre line, code scrolls inside its own box and tables scroll in a wrapper, and all of it is valid CSS with no repeated magic numbers. Answer B is leaner, with only two breakpoints, but it has real bugs: in its own usage example neither the `.bleed` div nor the `pre` gets `overflow-x`, so long code lines spill out. Its 100vw bleed can also cause horizontal overflow, and it adds a hard-coded `4rem` gap and a global `min-width` on every table. A is somewhat heavier than needed, with four breakpoints and separate classes for 3- and 4-tier pricing. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B's CSS works as described: code blocks scroll inside their own box, tables get a scroll wrapper, and prose and wide blocks are centered on the same axis using named tokens. A has a real bug: `.bleed:is(pre)` never matches because the bleed element is a div, so long code lines inside `pre` have no `overflow-x` and can overflow. A also hardcodes a 4rem feature gap and lets pricing sit at 2 columns, which orphans the third card. B adds a few more breakpoints and tokens than strictly needed, but it is the more correct and more complete answer overall.
